definition: Primeval means belonging to the earliest, most ancient period of the world; primitive and original.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word primeval. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know primeval should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Mist drifted between the giant ferns, giving the swamp a primeval look, as if dinosaurs might still wade through it.
An age-old custom stretches back many generations, while something primeval belongs to the earliest era of the world itself.
Primeval describes the world's first ages, but primordial reaches back even further, to the very beginning of existence, before life had fully taken shape.

Primal means first in time, original and instinctive - primal fear, primal urges, the primal state of things. It points inward at the drives we started with. Primeval points outward at the world's own first ages: forests and oceans that existed before civilization. A scream can be primal; a landscape is primeval.

Ancient means dating from the distant past, and human history is enough for ancient - ancient Rome, an ancient custom, an ancient map. Primeval reaches far past any civilization to the earliest era of the world itself, before people existed to record it. A two-thousand-year-old road is ancient; an untouched forest older than humanity is primeval.
